groups.cache_relation: At each request, old and new models encode exactly the same complete causal history prefix capped at 1024. Rebuild reads target-model KV with target parameters; Reuse reads cache-source-model KV with target parameters.
groups.reliability: Positive NDCG@10 difference with nominal user-level 95% interval entirely above zero; Recall@10 also positive.
reliability_limits: Selected from nine evaluated adjacent pairs after seeing their results; this is retained development evidence, not an independent confirmation set.
The 95% interval is a paired user-cluster bootstrap for request-macro NDCG@10; nominal per-pair coverage, no multiple-comparison correction.
Same fixed training-user cohort evaluated strictly after the target model cutoff; shared users/checkpoints make groups statistically dependent.
Matched causal-prefix snapshots, not persistent-cache/FIFO serving; prior observed test feedback may enter subsequent histories causally.
Observed-positive relevance over complete logged candidate sets; unexposed candidates are unknown, not observed negative feedback.
Only one complete future-day window is currently recorded per group; stability across additional windows is not established.

experiment_journal.question: Does a two-day publication interval M3 to M5 produce a positive cache-reuse loss on the unchanged next-day ranking task?

decision.question: Two-day release M3 to M5 on unchanged next full day
decision.interpretation: Negative point estimate with interval crossing zero; inconclusive for small effects, no promising positive signal to justify full expansion.
decision.next_action: One same-size two-day-release control M1 to M3 in an earlier training period; no new training and no automatic queue

experiment_journal.question: Does the same two-day publication interval show a positive cache gap in an earlier training period, after the M3 to M5 pilot was inconclusive?

decision.question: Two-day publication in earlier training period M1 to M3
decision.interpretation: Positive NDCG relative loss 2.0777% and positive Recall@10; nominal CI narrowly crosses zero. Promising pilot, not counted as a validated new pair yet.
decision.next_action: One disjoint UID replication: permutation positions4096:12288 (8192 users), same models and D31 full day, all requests and candidates retained.

experiment_journal.question: Does the promising M1 to M3 two-day-release NDCG loss reproduce on the next8192 disjoint fixed training users with the same complete-day window?

decision.question: Does the M1 to M3 pilot cache gap replicate on a larger disjoint user sample on the same complete future day?
decision.interpretation: Positive 2.6608% NDCG loss, positive Recall loss; both predetermined UID halves and both 12-hour halves are positive. Nominal UID95 interval excludes zero. Same models and day, disjoint users; not independent training or time replication.
decision.next_action: Register fifth usable model pair using replication-alone primary metrics; test only M2 to M4 pilot4096 as next two-day publication case.

experiment_journal.question: Does the same two-day publication interval produce a reproducible cache-reuse loss on the next target, M4, after M1 to M3 replicated positively on disjoint users?

decision.question: Two-day M2 to M4 publication on unchanged next complete day D32
decision.interpretation: Positive NDCG relative loss4.1344%, Recall4.3166%, all predetermined user/time slices positive. Effect exceeds preferred1–3% range; retain actual value and assess disjoint replication without tuning.
decision.next_action: One disjoint8192 UID replication at permutation4096:12288, same M2/M4 and D32 full day. If positive, register sixth usable pair and stop searching.

experiment_journal.question: Does the M2 to M4 two-day publication gap reproduce on 8192 disjoint users, keeping the same complete D32 window and full candidates?

decision.question: Does M2 to M4 replicate on8192 disjoint users on unchanged complete D32?
decision.interpretation: Positive replication NDCG loss2.8778%, Recall2.7086%, nominal user95 interval positive; both predetermined user halves and both12h halves positive. Pilot4.1344% retained separately, primary replication alone. Six distinct usable ordered model pairs now available, correlated rather than independent training experiments.
decision.next_action: Stop exploration; no successor experiments. Final semantic/path/metric/evidence inventory and handoff only.

limitations: These are selected mechanism cases, not an unbiased estimate of how often cache reuse loses quality.
Original 30,000-user results were already observed under immediate-parent reuse. New replication users are disjoint from their pilots, not globally unseen users.
Groups share checkpoints, users or dates. Disjoint-user replication is not independent retraining, another random seed or an independent calendar window.
New-group primary metrics use replication alone; pilot results are reported separately and are not pooled or selected by maximum effect.
Nominal user-cluster confidence intervals are informational; no universal CI threshold or multiplicity-adjusted population claim is made.
Means over the selected positive pairs are descriptive only. Preferred 1–3% effects were not enforced and larger observed values were retained.
All comparisons preserve full logged candidate sets, shared requests and causal histories up to 1024; this is matched-prefix snapshot replay, not persistent-cache/FIFO serving.
Zero-positive requests are counted but omitted from undefined NDCG/Recall means; unexposed items have unknown relevance.
verification: Existing completed audits, semantic model paths, full-window records, chosen-UID disjointness and registry numerical consistency; raw numerical scoring was not repeated.
